# Multi-window dock transactions, topology, and reload

## Goal

A user can move panes and popup workspaces across real browser windows, undo and redo those actions through one app-level history, save the resulting multi-window composition, and reload into the same topology without replaying history. A single-window application remains the one-workspace case and loads no transaction/history module when `historyDepth: 0`.

This needs an Epic because the outcome crosses persisted wire authority, App-Worker identity, collection-backed history, multi-participant commit atomicity, main-thread window effects, Neural Link commands, projection, Workstation controls, and end-to-end recovery. Each implementation unit must remain one-PR-deliverable; the native parent-child graph is the leaf registry.

## Problem Scope

The current system has rich dock primitives but no aggregate owner:

- `WorkspaceDocument.commit()` prepares one document at a time; the current reverse record is single-holder.
- `appName` identifies an application type, not one logical root. Independent Workstation roots can share one SharedWorker and collide on static workspace/drag identifiers.
- `windowId` changes on reload, while semantic workspace membership and history must survive a warm reload.
- the landed topology envelope is positional and sibling projections do not converge;
- popup movement is observable through `manager.Window`, but requested native effects are not durable truth;
- dock undo is split between a Neural Link-private stack and ordinary UI paths that record nothing;
- consumers persist partial live-layout state independently and no Workstation undo/redo surface exists.

The source Discussion resolved those as one ownership problem rather than local callbacks.

## Intended Solution Shape

`Neo.manager.Transaction` is a collection-backed singleton registry of logical Groups. Each Group owns semantic workspace bindings, bounded append-only history, one cursor, current durable topology state, and a `state.Provider` surface for `canUndo` / `canRedo`. The authoritative history is a `collection.Base` of recursively frozen plain records; any `data.Store` is a lazy read-only projection, never a second authority.

Identity has four non-collapsible coordinates:

| Coordinate | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `appName` | application type and routing label |
| `groupId` | one logical topology instance |
| `workspaceKey` | one semantic workspace/window slot |
| `windowId` | one replaceable browser-document generation |

Bindings are `(groupId, workspaceKey) → {windowId, generationToken}`; unregister is token-matched. Main-thread boot injects the root carrier into the App Worker, same-origin popups inherit the Group, and independent same-app roots mint different Groups.

A Group write is serialized as: prepare every participant → adopt all with compensation → append one immutable transaction → move the cursor → publish one topology snapshot → release the queue. Projection and native effect receipts remain separate. A popup move records observed relative `{dx,dy}`; a main-window move re-bases popup hints without advancing history.

Warm F5 rebinds to the surviving Group and retains cursor/history without replay. Cold boot creates a new Group, hydrates one durable snapshot, starts with empty history, and materializes popup slots only behind user activation. Refusal preserves headless semantic participants and a user-visible recovery path.

The hard persisted cut keeps `neo.dock.zone.v1` and the single-workspace meanings of `neo.dock.layout.v1` / `neo.dock.layoutCollection.v1`, introduces keyed `neo.dock.topology.v1` / `neo.dock.topologyCollection.v1`, and deletes positional topology fields/readers. There is no compatibility reader, alias, or migration path.

## Structural Placement

`src/manager/Transaction.mjs` matches the collection-backed singleton pattern established by `manager.Base`, `manager.Store`, and `manager.Window`. Generic Group/history classes belong under `src/manager/transaction/`; dock-specific participant adapters remain under `src/dashboard/dock/`. The manager layer must not import dock concepts, and `DragCoordinator` remains dock-blind.

The Engine-local `ai:structure-map` command no longer exists; it was executed and returned no output with exit 1. Placement authority is therefore the current Runtime Engine inventory plus ADR 0029 and the named siblings. Because the Runtime Engine inventory has no `src/manager/` row, the first structurally significant manager delivery must update it.

Scalability: the namespace can hold additional transaction domains without turning `src/manager/` into a flat junk drawer. ADR conflict: ADR 0029 is amended before implementation. ADR genesis: none; the accepted ADR already owns this cross-system trade-off. Future-self risk: generic manager contracts stay free of DockLayouts imports, while domain adapters retain their existing home.

- Criteria 6 and 13 become logical Group identity, token-matched generation rebind, duplicate-root fork, and warm-versus-cold lifecycle.

- Criterion 10 becomes strict cross-Group drag isolation before any user-visible target effect.

- The consumer-level proof becomes the end-to-end Workstation save/reload/undo journey.

## Decision Record Impact

Decision Record impact: **amends ADR 0029**. The amendment is merge-ordered before every consuming implementation and replaces its positional topology/persistence contract only where D#18224 explicitly says so.

## Decision Record

**Required: amend ADR 0029.** The same freeze truth-syncs `DockZoneModel.md`, `NeuralLinkCapabilityMatrix.md`, the DockLayouts guide, and all shipped positional readers. No competing ADR.

## Out of Scope

- Cross-Group or cross-application drag support. The v13.2 contract is isolation; a bridge is deferred until after the single-Group manager ships.
- History replay on cold boot or undo across cold boot.
- Absolute screen coordinates, monitor ids, `DOMRect`, `windowId`, live components, or credentials in persisted JSON.
- `appName` as implicit Group identity.
- A mutable Model/Store as history authority.
- Compatibility aliases, migration readers, or parallel old/new schema paths.
- Re-solving Workspace decomposition owned by D#18150; only the settled Group destination is shared.

## Avoided Traps

- Adding a second dock undo stack beside the Neural Link stack.
- Recording inside `WorkspaceDocument.commit()`, which lacks Group/origin/effect context.
- Treating requested native window operations as committed truth.
- Concatenating `sortGroup` and ownership identity.
- Destroying a Workspace to unregister one window generation.
- Disarming realm-wide geometry observation when one binding leaves.
- Loading history machinery into a single-window/history-disabled app.
- Proving the lazy-load boundary with only module count or only bytes; #18310 must preserve both zero loads and byte-equivalent single-window closure.
- Replaying prose through another Discussion round instead of shipping linked leaves.

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-09-05T19:57:42Z

Follow-up to the criterion-10 obstacle above — the cause is measured and it is a product defect, filed as #18376.

Root B's sparkline canvases are transferred as OffscreenCanvases to the App Worker, a SharedWorker hosted in root A's renderer process; Chromium terminates that process for the cross-process frame sink ("Invalid client ID"), which is why A dies and B boots. Discriminator: with `transferControlToOffscreen` made to throw in B only, both roots stay alive and A still answers; made to throw in A only, A dies as before. It is the same kill Electron documents for an OffscreenCanvas crossing an out-of-process boundary. Pop-out vessels are unaffected because a popup joins its opener's process; an unrelated tab of the same origin does not.

Consequence for this epic: two independent full roots cannot coexist in the product today wherever they land in separate processes, so the rendered two-root journey waits on #18376's fix shape, which is a worker-topology decision for the worker manager's owner. The witness at PR #18368 stays the receipt that exists.
